modules.comments:
One shared "flow" value: things that hold a value (items) and things that
compute (steps), wired together, as in Build Systems a la Carte's store
and tasks. Domain detail rides in the `item`, `step` and `wire`
parameters and is never inspected here. A flow with nothing to say about
its wires has `Unit` there; one whose wires carry a quantity (a Sankey's
widths) has the quantity.

What is drawn is not in the value: `project` takes a `Drawing`. Run state
is not in the value: see `Hylograph.Flow.Overlay`. Grouping is not in the
value: see `Hylograph.Flow.Grouping`. Shapes of steps over collections
live one layer up, in `Hylograph.Flow.Collection`.

declarations.comments:
Which item. `ItemId`: an item of the source, by the name the source gave
it. `GroupItem`: the summary item of a closed group under `collapse`,
which stands for what the group provides to the rest of the flow. They
are different constructors, as a step's are, so no name a source can give
an item is the identity of a group's summary.
declarations.title: ItemId

declarations.comments:
Which step. `StepId`: a step of the source, by the name the source gave
it. `GroupStep`: the one step a closed group became under `collapse`.
They are different constructors, so no name a source can give a step is
the identity of a group, whatever the name's letters.
declarations.title: StepId

declarations.comments:
Which port of a step. `PortName`: a port of the source's own step.
`MemberPort`: a port of a closed group, which is a port of one of its
members seen from outside: the member and the member's port. The member
may itself be a closed group and its port a `MemberPort`, where a flow
already collapsed is collapsed again. `SummaryPort`: the port by which a
closed group meets a group's summary item: its own, which it writes by
it, or another closed group's, which it reads by it. (A step that is no
closed group reads a summary item by its own port.)
declarations.title: PortName

declarations.comments:
Which group, of a grouping beside a flow (`Hylograph.Flow.Grouping`).
Here, and not there, because a closed group's step, its summary item and
the port between them are named by it.
declarations.title: GroupId

declarations.comments:
A step's id as words for a reader: the source's name, or `group:` and
the group's. For display only: two different ids can read the same (a
step the source named `group:G` and the closed group `G`), so nothing
is to be keyed or compared by it.
declarations.title: stepLabel

declarations.comments:
An item's id as words for a reader: the source's name, or `group:` and
the group's. For display only, as `stepLabel` is.
declarations.title: itemLabel

declarations.comments:
A port as words for a reader: the source's name, or the member's label,
a dot, and the member's port, or `summary:` and the group's name. For
display only, as `stepLabel` is.
declarations.title: portLabel

declarations.comments:
What holds a value: a column, a file, a stream, a store. `name` is
`Nothing` only where the source gives the thing no name (a radio
stream, a chart's link). `count`: how many values it holds side by side.
declarations.title: Item

declarations.comments: What computes.
declarations.title: Step

declarations.comments:
Which wire: its two ends and the port at the step end. This is a wire's
whole identity; what it carries is no part of it.
declarations.title: WireId

declarations.comments:
A wire and what it carries, shaped as an item and a step are: an id and
a payload. The payload is `Unit` where there is nothing to say.
declarations.title: Wire

declarations.comments: A wire that carries nothing.
declarations.title: plain

declarations.comments: The two elements a wire joins, in the direction it runs.
declarations.title: wireEnds

declarations.comments: A freshly imported flow and what the importer found that does not fit.
declarations.title: Imported

declarations.comments:
Any element of a flow, for drawing and for overlays. A wire is keyed by
its identity, never by what it carries.
declarations.title: ElementKey

declarations.comments:
Which elements a picture draws as nodes. Every element not drawn is
contracted: an edge runs between two drawn elements for each path of
wires between them through undrawn ones.

- `Holders`: items are nodes, each step becomes edges (a spreadsheet's
  columns, a Makefile's files).
- `Steps`: steps are nodes, each item becomes edges (a radio's blocks).
- `Both`: the bipartite graph, every wire an edge.
- `Chosen`: the caller says, element by element. Added beyond the three
  agreed cases, because two subjects (Makefile phony targets drawn
  among files; the rig chart's stores drawn among its processes) draw
  some of each kind, and none of the three reproduces them.
declarations.title: Drawing

declarations.comments: Whether a drawing draws an element as a node.
declarations.title: drawnBy

declarations.comments:
A drawn element. `label`: its name, or its id where it has none.
`inputs`, `outputs`: a step's ports (empty for an item).
declarations.title: Node

declarations.comments:
`via`: the undrawn elements the edge passes through, from source to
target. `fromPort`: the port it leaves a drawn step by; `toPort`: the
port it enters a drawn step by. `wires`: the wires the edge stands for,
each with its identity and what it carries, from source to target. They
are a path: the first leaves `from`, the last enters `to`, and each one
between meets the next at an element of `via`. An edge is at least one
wire: exactly one where the edge is a wire (`Both`), two where it
crosses one undrawn element. A wire on several paths is in several
edges. (`Hylograph.Flow.Laws` states all of this as a function.)
declarations.title: Edge

declarations.comments:
Nodes in array order, items before steps. Edges in the order of the
wire that enters their target.
declarations.title: project

declarations.comments:
Every wire names an existing item, step and port; each item has at most
one writer; ids are unique, a wire's too (two wires with one identity
could not be told apart by an overlay).

In order: items said twice, steps said twice, wires said twice (each
once, in the order first met); then what is wrong with each wire, wire
by wire; then the items written twice.
declarations.title: problems

declarations.comments:
Longest path from a node with no incoming edge, over the projection.
Self-loops are ignored; nodes on a cycle get the layer they had when
the cycle was met.
declarations.title: layers

declarations.comments:
Per node, the set of nodes with no incoming edge that reach it (itself,
for such a node).
declarations.title: leafMass

declarations.comments: Nodes no edge touches, in node order.
declarations.title: isolated

modules.name: Hylograph.Flow

modules.comments:
One layer up from the flow: a step payload for flows over collections.
A step is one of the five familiar operations, or explicitly none of
them, carrying the domain's own description of what it is instead.

declarations.comments: `detail`: the domain's own data for the step (a formula, a recipe).
declarations.title: CollectionStep

modules.name: Hylograph.Flow.Collection

modules.comments:
Grouping beside a flow, never in it: a nested partition of the flow's
steps and items (a rose tree whose leaves are steps and items), and
`collapse`, which draws a cut through it and gives the coarser flow.

## What a group names

`Member` names a step and `Holds` names an item; a `Group` holds either,
and groups. A grouping is well formed when every step, every item and
every group id is in it at most once (`groupingProblems` says what is
not). Nothing ties an item's group to its writer's: a table of entered
data has no writer and belongs to its sheet; a module's output belongs to
its package; an item may be held by one group and written by a step of
another. An item no group holds is treated as 0.1 treated every item (see
the last rule below), so a grouping of steps alone means what it meant.

## What a closed group is, in the coarser flow

The core has two kinds of node and wires only between the two kinds, and
`collapse` keeps to that. A closed group becomes

- **one step**, `GroupStep` of its id, carrying the payloads of every
  step and every item shut inside it (`Closed`); and
- **at most one item**, its *summary*, `GroupItem` of its id: what the
  group provides. It is there exactly when something leaves the group
  through an item, and it is written by the group's step and by nothing
  else, so the one-writer rule holds of it by construction.

Which side of the cut an element is on:

- a step under a closed group is inside it (the outermost closed group
  over it; an open group is transparent);
- an item a closed group holds is inside it, unless an open step writes
  it. An item written by a step that stays drawn stays drawn: it is the
  one thing that can stand between that step and the group, since a wire
  joins an item and a step, and it is not invented;
- an item no closed group holds is inside a closed group only as in 0.1:
  when that group writes it, and it is read, and read only there.

And then every wire of the finer flow is exactly one of these:

| the wire | in the coarser flow |
|---|---|
| both ends inside one closed group | gone: it is inside the group |
| neither end inside a closed group | itself |
| a step inside `G`, an item that stays | the same wire at `GroupStep G`, by the member's port (`MemberPort`); parallel ones merged, as in 0.1 |
| an item inside `G` read by a step outside `G` | a read of `G`'s summary: by the reader's own port, or by `SummaryPort G` where the reader is itself a closed group's step |
| an item inside `G` written by a step inside another closed group `H` | a read of `H`'s summary by `GroupStep G`, at `SummaryPort H` |

Wires left with one identity are merged, their payloads combined with
`<>` in wire order. A summary's one write wire carries the combination of
every wire that became a read of it: what a group provides is what is
taken from it. No wire of the coarser flow is invented: each stands for
at least one wire of the finer flow, which is why `Semigroup` is enough.

So what crosses a group's boundary is conserved. The wires of the finer
flow with one end inside `G` and one outside are, payload for payload,
the wires of the coarser flow that join `G`'s step or summary to anything
else (the summary's own write wire is inside the group's two nodes and
repeats what the reads of it carry).

Between two closed groups `G` and `H`, everything that goes from `G` to
`H` through items inside either is one wire, `Reads (GroupItem G)
(GroupStep H) (SummaryPort G)`. Under `Steps` that is one edge from `G`
to `H`, and one from `H` to `G` where each reads the other: a cycle
between two closed groups is two edges, neither dropped. Under `Both` a
providing group is its step, its summary, and the wire between; under
`Holders` it is its summary alone, with an edge from every summary and
item it reads, and a group that provides nothing is no node (as a step
that writes nothing is no edge). A second edge between two closed groups
can only run through an item that stayed drawn, which is an item no
closed group holds.

## Identities

`GroupStep`, `GroupItem`, `MemberPort` and `SummaryPort` are constructors
no step, item or port of a source has. So whatever the source's elements
are called, none is taken for a group's, and a flow already collapsed can
be collapsed again: a `Member` may name a `GroupStep` and a `Holds` a
`GroupItem`. (The one thing left to the caller: a second cut must not
reuse the id of a group the first cut closed, unless it holds that
group's step.)

One mechanism for a radio's fused runs, for semantic zoom, for the rig
chart's machines opened into their voices, for a workbook by sheet and a
workspace by package.

declarations.comments: A step, an item, or a named group of groupings.
declarations.title: Grouping

declarations.comments:
A step of the coarser flow: one kept as it was, or a closed group with
the payloads of everything shut inside it: its steps in step order, and
its items in item order. Every step of the finer flow is kept or is in
exactly one closed group's `steps`, and every item is kept or is in
exactly one closed group's `items`.
declarations.title: Collapsed

declarations.comments:
An item of the coarser flow: one kept as it was, or a closed group's
summary with the payloads of the items it stands for, in item order:
those inside the group that something outside reads, and those inside
another closed group that this group writes. There is always one, since
a summary is there only when something leaves through it.
declarations.title: CollapsedItem

declarations.comments: What keeps a forest from being a partition.
declarations.title: GroupingProblem

declarations.comments: Every step under a grouping.
declarations.title: members

declarations.comments: Every item under a grouping.
declarations.title: held

declarations.comments:
A forest is well formed when no step, no item and no group id is in it
twice. (`collapse` is total even so: where a forest puts an element
under two closed groups, it is in the later one.)
declarations.title: groupingProblems

declarations.comments:
The coarser flow for a cut: the groups in `closed` are drawn shut; a
closed group shuts everything under it; an open one is transparent. The
module's header says what each element and each wire becomes.

Parallel wires are merged: where several members of a closed group read
one item that stays visible, the group reads it by one wire, at the port
of the first of them, carrying what they carried, combined in wire order.
(Likewise for writes, and for any two wires left with one identity.) The
group keeps no port for a wire merged away. So between a closed group
and an item there is at most one wire each way, and no two wires of the
coarser flow share an identity.

Order: the items that stay, in item order, then the summaries in the
order of their groups in the forest. A closed group's step stands where
the first of its member steps stood; one with no step of the flow under
it (a group of items only) comes after every other step, in forest
order. A closed group with nothing of the flow inside it is no step.
Wires in the order of the first wire each stands for, a summary's write
just before the first read of it.

`Semigroup`, not a function argument: the merge has to be associative
for the result not to depend on how the wires happen to be bracketed,
which is the one law the class states, and `Unit` already has it.
declarations.title: collapse

declarations.comments: The step a closed group becomes.
declarations.title: groupStep

declarations.comments: The summary item of a closed group: what it provides.
declarations.title: groupItem

modules.name: Hylograph.Flow.Grouping

declarations.comments:
Which group, of a grouping beside a flow (`Hylograph.Flow.Grouping`).
Here, and not there, because a closed group's step, its summary item and
the port between them are named by it.
declarations.title: GroupId

modules.comments:
INTERNAL: no part of the library's interface, and free to change in any
release. The three ways the library's own functions look a flow's
arrays up without scanning them again for every element: values gathered
under a key, how often each value occurs, and which occur more than once.

declarations.comments:
Every value under its key, a key's values in the order they came.
One sort by key and then by place, so that nothing rests on the sort's
being stable and no array is appended to once for each value.
declarations.title: gathered

declarations.comments: What was gathered under a key; nothing, where the key was never met.
declarations.title: under

declarations.comments: How many times each value occurs.
declarations.title: tally

declarations.comments:
The values that occur more than once, each once, in the order of their
first occurrence.
declarations.title: repeated

modules.name: Hylograph.Flow.Internal.Index

modules.comments:
What must hold of any projection of any flow, as a function that returns
what does not. Here, and not in a test directory, so that every adapter's
tests can hold the projections of its own real flows to it.

declarations.comments:
Every fault in the projection of a flow under a drawing, in words; none
is the law.

- every wire of every edge is a wire of the flow;
- an edge's wires are a path: the first leaves `from`, the last enters
  `to`, each one between meets the next at the element of `via` in that
  place, both ends are drawn and nothing in `via` is; `fromPort` and
  `toPort` are the ports of the first and last wire where those ends
  are steps;
- the edges are exactly the paths of wires from a drawn element to a
  drawn element through undrawn ones (`paths`), each path one edge.

So a wire between two drawn elements is one edge, alone in it; a wire
with an undrawn end is in one edge for each such path through it, which
may be several (a step with two inputs, contracted, puts its output
wire in two edges) or none (nothing drawn is reached that way). Those
two are restated as checks of their own, though they follow.
declarations.title: projectionFaults

declarations.comments:
Every path of wires from a drawn element to a drawn element through
undrawn ones, no undrawn element twice on a path. Found walking forwards
from each wire that leaves a drawn element, where `project` walks
backwards from each wire that enters one.
declarations.title: paths

modules.name: Hylograph.Flow.Laws

modules.comments:
Run state beside a flow, never in it: anything known about any element
(a file stale, a link broken, a step running), keyed by the element.
